source.title: Two Speeds of Learning: A Representation-Readout Decomposition of Grokking and Double Descent
source.authors: Chi-Ning Chou; Oscar Uzdelewicz; Neng-Chun Chiu; Yao-Yuan Yang; SueYeon Chung

record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly reproduces epoch-wise double descent by training a ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with varying label-noise levels and tracking generalization over epochs.
record.gate_note: The paper tests epoch-wise double descent and its dependence on label noise. It reports the trajectories in figures and describes their qualitative patterns in text, but gives no numeric test-error values. Cited results about model-wise double descent and other studies are not this paper's results and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reruns Nakkiran et al.'s epoch-wise double-descent setup and reports whether the test-accuracy dip appears. The setup is ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with 0/10/20% label noise, Adam at lr 1e-4 with no weight decay, for 4,000 epochs. Its own results bear on V2 and on the noise dependence in V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one omission. The authors also frame label-noise double descent as 'spurious', an artifact of a non-standard training recipe. Under that framing, it arises from representation deterioration in the valley followed by readout updates dominated by noisy labels. Removing the noise removes both the double descent and the diagnostic signatures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses label corruption and an epoch-wise generalization sweep, explicitly to reproduce the reported phenomenon; this paper specifies a CIFAR-10 ResNet18, 0%, 10%, and 20% noise, and its own training setup. Exact equivalence to the original recipe is not established in the text.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported double-descent pattern depends on label-noise level: it is absent at 0% noise and becomes more pronounced as noise increases across the tested levels.

fits_no_version.finding: During the test-accuracy descent, three things happen together: linear-probe accuracy plateaus, critical dimension Ncrit rises, and NTK-label alignment falls. In the recovery phase, alignment with the noisy train labels exceeds alignment with clean labels. A linear probe on clean labels beats the model's own accuracy throughout. None of these signatures appear at 0% noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise double descent under label noise reflects degradation of the learned representation followed by the readout fitting the noisy labels, rather than a property of genuine generalization.

record.problems: The double-descent outcomes are reported qualitatively from figures, without numeric test-error values in the text. The text does not state uncertainty estimates for these trajectories.

untested.parts: Other architectures, other datasets and model widths; test loss as opposed to accuracy; how robust the result is across seeds.
Splitting into multiple peaks (triple descent); removal of the peak under optimally tuned regularization (weight decay is fixed at 0); noise levels above 20%.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict where the peak falls.

record.verdict_notes: The recipe nearly matches the epoch-wise setup in Nakkiran et al. (ResNet18, Adam 1e-4, 4k epochs, 0/10/20% noise). The width is not stated beyond the 512-dimensional feature vector. All double-descent evidence is in figures (Figs 7, 28-30), with no numbers, seed count or error bars. The record's 'challenges' label for V2 at 0% noise was downgraded to limits_scope: V2 does not claim the effect appears without noise, and the originals emphasise the noise setting. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error comparison across model sizes.
Tested only for a ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 across the reported label-noise settings; no other architectures or datasets are tested for epoch-wise double descent.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison across model classes or capacity sweep past an interpolation point.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Tests dependence on label-noise level. Does not test multiple or split peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameter number or test of whether that converts second descent into an ordinary U-shape.

relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell, rose, and fell again at both 10% and 20% label noise.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: R2 and R3 support epoch-wise double descent. The supplied rationale reverses accuracy's direction: fall-rise-fall describes test error; the corresponding accuracy trajectory is rise-fall-rise.

relationships.reason: With clean labels the authors state double descent is absent and accuracy rises monotonically (R1). So the epoch-wise shape depends on label noise in this setup. The original also mainly reported it under noise, so this qualifies V2 rather than refuting it.
relationships.display_finding: With 0% label noise, accuracy rose monotonically and epoch-wise double descent was absent.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R1 explicitly lacks double descent; Appendix D.4 states validation accuracy increases monotonically after memorization. The clean control qualifies the noisy-label result.

relationships.reason: The dip is absent at 0% noise, present at 10%, and more pronounced at 20% (R1-R3). This fits a peak driven by label noise.
relationships.display_finding: The dip was absent at 0% label noise, appeared at 10%, and became more pronounced at 20%.

source_check.label: supports
